original_query: select empno, sum(sal), min(sal), max(sal),  bit_and(distinct sal), bit_or(sal), count(distinct sal),  grouping(deptno) from emp group by empno, deptno
rewritten_query:
SELECT
    empno,
    sal::bigint AS "sum",
    sal AS "min",
    sal AS "max",
    sal AS "bit_and",
    sal AS "bit_or",
    CASE WHEN sal IS NULL THEN 0::bigint ELSE 1::bigint END AS "count",
    0 AS "grouping"
FROM emp;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: grouping(deptno) is always 0 because deptno appears in the GROUP BY clause, so it can be replaced with the constant 0.

empno is the primary key (emp_pkey), so deptno is functionally dependent on empno and each group contains exactly one row. All aggregates therefore degenerate to scalar expressions: sum(sal) becomes sal::bigint, min/max/bit_and/bit_or become sal, and count(distinct sal) becomes a NULL-aware CASE expression. This eliminates GroupAggregate and the Incremental Sort on (empno, sal) over 45M rows.
No subqueries exist; the main optimization is removing the redundant aggregation and DISTINCT processing entirely.
